kept.q: Which of the following best describes soil fertility?
options: The capacity of soil to supply nutrients needed for healthy crop growth
The weight of soil particles per hectare
The number of earthworms found in a soil sample
The colour of the topsoil layer
kept.explanation: Soil fertility refers to the ability of soil to provide the nutrients and conditions that crops need to grow well. The other options do not define fertility.
kept.pidgin: Soil fertility na how di soil fit give di nutrients wey crop need to grow well. Di oda options no dey explain fertility at all.

kept.q: A farmer in Benue State notices that her maize farm has poor growth even though she applies fertilizer regularly. Which of the following is NOT a likely cause of continued low fertility?
options: Severe leaching of nutrients on sandy soil
Continuous cropping without rest
Planting a legume like cowpea before maize
Removal of topsoil through erosion
kept.explanation: Planting a legume like cowpea before maize actually improves soil fertility through nitrogen fixation, so it is not a cause of low fertility. The other three options reduce soil fertility.
kept.pidgin: To plant legume like cowpea before maize dey add nitrogen to soil, e no dey cause low fertility. But di oda three things dey reduce di soil fertility well well.

kept.q: Which nutrient element in NPK fertilizer is most easily lost from the soil through leaching because it exists mainly as a soluble nitrate ion?
options: Nitrogen
Phosphorus
Potassium
Calcium
kept.explanation: Nitrogen, especially in the nitrate form (NO3-), dissolves easily in water and is washed down below the root zone, which is why it is most prone to leaching. Phosphorus and potassium are less mobile in soil.
kept.pidgin: Nitrogen, especially as nitrate, dey mix well well with water so rain fit wash am comot from where di roots dey. Phosphorus and potassium no dey move like that inside soil.

kept.q: A farmer applies fertilizer at the rate of 300 kg per hectare on his 4-hectare rice farm in Niger State. If each kilogram of the fertilizer costs ₦180, what is the total cost of fertilizer for the whole farm?
kept.explanation: Total fertilizer needed = 300 kg/ha x 4 ha = 1200 kg. Total cost = 1200 kg x ₦180 = ₦216,000.
kept.pidgin: Total fertilizer wey dem go need = 300kg x 4 hectare = 1200kg. Total money = 1200kg x ₦180 = ₦216,000.

kept.q: Which of the following farm practices helps to improve soil fertility while also reducing soil erosion on a sloppy farmland?
options: Planting cover crops such as centrosema
Bush burning before planting
Continuous monocropping of maize
Deep ploughing across the slope every season
kept.explanation: Cover crops like centrosema protect the soil surface from erosion while adding organic matter and nitrogen to improve fertility. Bush burning and monocropping instead reduce soil fertility over time.
kept.pidgin: Cover crop like centrosema dey cover di soil so erosion no go carry am, e dey also add organic matter and nitrogen go soil. Bush burning and monocropping dey spoil di soil instead.

kept.q: Farmyard manure is generally considered better than chemical fertilizer for long-term soil improvement mainly because it
options: improves soil structure and adds organic matter in addition to supplying nutrients
acts faster than chemical fertilizer in supplying nutrients to crops
contains a higher percentage of nitrogen than urea
is completely free of any disease-causing organisms
kept.explanation: Farmyard manure improves soil texture, water-holding capacity and adds humus while slowly releasing nutrients, which benefits the soil over a longer period. Chemical fertilizers act faster but do not improve soil structure.
kept.pidgin: Farmyard manure dey improve how di soil dey arrange and e dey add organic matter wey dey helep soil hold water, e dey release nutrients small small for long time. Chemical fertilizer dey work fast but e no dey improve soil structure.

kept.q: A crop that performs best in slightly acidic soil (pH 6.0-6.5) is being grown by a farmer who repeatedly applies ammonium sulphate fertilizer over several years. What long-term effect should the farmer expect on the soil pH?
options: The soil will become more acidic over time
The soil will become more alkaline over time
The soil pH will remain completely unchanged
The soil will become neutral regardless of the original pH
kept.explanation: Ammonium sulphate is an acid-forming fertilizer; repeated use releases hydrogen ions into the soil, lowering the pH and making the soil more acidic over time. This can eventually harm crops that need near-neutral conditions.
kept.pidgin: Ammonium sulphate na fertilizer wey dey make soil acidic small small as farmer dey use am plenty times, e dey release hydrogen ions wey dey lower di pH. If dem no control am, e fit spoil crop wey need pH wey no too acidic.
